author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Salem Police Chief Lucas Miller is marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks by returning to Ground Zero, where he will join a ceremony and reconnect with detectives he worked alongside as a New York City police officer.

Miller was an NYPD detective heading to court on September 11, 2001, when the first plane struck the World Trade Center. He recalled jammed traffic and confusion in the streets before contacting his command and receiving an assignment.

Detectives were sent to nearby hospitals to locate victims and potential suspects, but Miller said the expected stream of patients never arrived. He later served with the Joint Terrorism Task Force from the FBI’s New York field office, work that strengthened coordination among local, state and federal agencies.

Miller ordinarily attends Salem’s memorial outside fire headquarters. This year, he plans to take part in Friday’s Ground Zero observance before spending time with former colleagues. Salem’s own tribute is also scheduled for Friday morning. His account connects the national anniversary to local public-safety leadership and to the long-term changes in interagency preparedness that followed the attacks.
dek: Lucas Miller was heading to court when the first tower was struck; he later searched hospitals for victims and suspects and served on a federal terrorism task force.
headline: Salem police chief recalls September 11 work as NYPD detective
